summary: Kazuaki Komine specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1967-1987) and held posts at Waseda Jitsugyo High School (1974), Tokushima University (1979), the National Institute of Japanese Literature (1984), and Rikkyo University (1995-2013).

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology, Kazuaki Tanahashi studied under Soichi Nakamura. He served as a scholar in residence at the San Francisco Zen Center (1977-1984) and is a fellow at the World Academy of Art and Science.

Kazufumi Oki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University. His academic career includes serving as an assistant professor (attested 1982-1990) and professor emeritus (attested 2006-2013) at Shuchiin University.

Kazuharu Mizuno works in Tibetology and other fields. He studied at Nagoya University (~1977-1982), Hokkaido University (~1982-1984), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1984-1989), later serving as a geography professor at Kyoto University (~2012).

Kazuhiko Atsumi worked in philosophy and other fields. After studying at the University of Tokyo (~1948-1954), he held positions at the University of Tokyo (~1964-1989) and Suzuka University of Medical Science (~1991-1998).

Kazuhiko Yoshida specializes in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Sophia, Cornell, Kyoto, and Osaka universities under Jay Jasanoff and Teizo Iyanaga, later holding posts at Nagoya City Women's College (~1989-1994) and Nagoya City University (2021-2024).
Kazuhiro Kaneiwa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held an attested post at Bukkyo University in 2001 and 2013.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kazuhiro Kawasaki completed his doctoral studies at Koyasan University. He has held positions at Koyasan University as a researcher (attested 2005) and special appointment professor (attested 2026).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).
Kazumi Yoshizaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Toyo University and held an attested post at the National Museum of Ethnology in 2001.

Kazunobu Matsuda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Shiro Matsumoto and at Otani University, where he also taught (attested 1985-1989), before serving as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1995-2024).

Kazuo Hyodo specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and at Otani University under Hajime Sakurabe, later serving as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1983-2014).

Kazuo Kano is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Hamburg. He has held posts at the University of Hamburg, Kyoto University, Koyasan University, and Komazawa University.
Kazuo Matsumura works in religious studies and Indology. After studying at Hitotsubashi University (~1972-1977), he held posts at Tenri University (~1987-2004) and Wako University (~2004).

Kazuo Okabe was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. Educated at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo, he held posts at the Institute for Zen Studies (1969) and Komazawa University, serving as professor from 1979 to 2006.

Kazuo Osumi specializes in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo (~1951-1964), he served as an assistant professor at Hokkaido University (1964) and professor at Tokyo Woman's Christian University (1977-2001).
Kazuo Oyamada works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tamagawa University and held a post at Rissho University.
Kazutoshi Soma is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a position as a lecturer at Ryukoku University (attested 1987).

Kazuyoshi Hotta specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies and held an administrative post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), and later held a post at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo (1942-1948). He founded Shinnyokai and served as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989) and vice-president of Shogen Junior College (1993).
